findings.title: Immediate email cancel neither retries nor records cancellation
findings.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true only POSTs a SendGrid batch cancel and then returns. It does not set WorkflowReminder.cancelled, nor delete the row. Reschedule (handleNewBooking.ts around the deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true) call), workflow deletion, and step deletion all use this path. That is the same SendGrid cancel that this PR says fails once 100 pending cancellations exist, and a failure is only logged. Because cancelled is never set, the new cron will not retry those batches, so rescheduled-booking reminder emails still go out — the bug the PR claims to fix. On success the row is also left behind with cancelled unset, so nothing later clears the scheduled_sends entry except the send time.

findings.title: Cron deletes due reminders before cancelling them at SendGrid
findings.body: The handler first deleteMany's every EMAIL WorkflowReminder whose scheduledDate is already <= now, then looks up cancelled reminders to POST a SendGrid cancel. Any cancelled reminder whose send time has passed, or passes before the next run, is removed from the database in that first query and is never sent to /v3/user/scheduled_sends. SendGrid still delivers it. The later cancel query cannot see those rows. Cancelled reminders inside the cron interval (about 15 minutes) have the same hole: they are only cancelled once they fall in the next-hour window, so a booking cancelled shortly before the reminder still sends.

findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the rest of the batch
findings.body: remindersToCancel is processed in a single try/catch. Each item awaits client.request with batch_id: reminder.referenceId and only then queues a delete. referenceId is not checked, and there is no per-item catch. The first 4xx/5xx (null batch id, already-cancelled batch, or the 100 pending-cancellation limit this PR is working around) jumps to the catch, skips Promise.all on the queued deletes, and never cancels later reminders in that run. If a poison row stays inside the one-hour window, every subsequent cron can fail at the same item and leave the other cancelled emails scheduled.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation is not awaited before the handler returns
findings.body: On booking cancel, deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder are started inside forEach and never awaited. The only thing that stops an already-scheduled email is the cancelled=true write inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder. The handler then awaits unrelated Prisma/calendar work and returns. On a serverless runtime the isolate can freeze after the response, so the update never commits and the cron never sees cancelled=true — the reminder is still sent. The same fire-and-forget pattern is in viewer/bookings.tsx requestReschedule and in handleNewBooking's reschedule block, whose try/catch cannot see those async failures because forEach does not await the promises.
